claim: The C. elegans genome encodes nine classical PUF proteins that cluster into four phylogenetic clades.
source: The C. elegans genome encodes nine classical PUF proteins that cluster into four phylogenetic clades (Figure 1A) (Stumpf et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stumpf et al., 2008 and reference to Figure 1A showing the dendrogram.

claim: Members of the FBF clade (FBF-1 and FBF-2) recognize the 9-nt FBF binding element or FBE, 5´-UGURNNAUA-3´.
source: Members of the FBF clade (FBF-1 and FBF-2) recognize the 9-nt FBF binding element or FBE, 5´-UGURNNAUA-3´ (Figure 1B) (Zhang et al., 1997; Bernstein, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 1997 and Bernstein, 2005, and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The clade containing PUF-8 and PUF-9 possesses a distinct specificity, and these proteins bind to the 8-nt PBE.
source: The clade containing PUF-8 and PUF-9 possesses a distinct specificity, and these proteins bind to the 8-nt PBE (Figure 1C) (Opperman et al., 2005; Nolde et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Opperman et al., 2005 and Nolde et al., 2007, and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: A 2.6 Å crystal structure of PUF-8 bound to an 8-nt PBE RNA, 5´-UGUAUAUA-3´ was determined.
source: To clarify the molecular basis of this divergent binding specificity, we determined a 2.6 Å crystal structure of PUF-8 bound to an 8-nt PBE RNA, 5´-UGUAUAUA-3´ (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing crystallographic statistics.

claim: The overall structure of the RNA-binding domain of PUF-8 is similar to that of other classical PUF proteins with eight α-helical PUM repeats (R1 to R8) and flanking regions at both the N- and C-termini (R1´ and R8´).
source: The overall structure of the RNA-binding domain of PUF-8 is similar to that of other classical PUF proteins with eight α-helical PUM repeats (R1 to R8) and flanking regions at both the N- and C-termini (R1´ and R8´; Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The eight repeats and two flanking regions together form a crescent shape, and the 8-nt RNA target sequence binds to the concave surface.
source: The eight repeats and two flanking regions together form a crescent shape, and the 8-nt RNA target sequence binds to the concave surface.
evidence: The claim is based on structural observations from the crystal structure.

claim: Target RNA bases are recognized by conserved amino acid side chains from PUF-8 repeats.
source: Target RNA bases are recognized by conserved amino acid side chains from PUF-8 repeats.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data showing protein-RNA interactions.

claim: The RNA binds with its 5´ end near the C-terminus of the protein.
source: The RNA binds with its 5´ end near the C-terminus of the protein (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PUM repeats R8-R5 bind to the 5´-UGUA sequence, and PUM repeats R3-R1 bind to bases 6–8, the AUA-3´ sequence.
source: PUM repeats R8-R5 bind to the 5´-UGUA sequence, and PUM repeats R3-R1 bind to bases 6–8, the AUA-3´ sequence (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: The 5´-UGUA and AUA-3´ base specific interactions bracket a central region in which the 5th base turns away from the concave RNA-binding surface and stacks directly with the 4th base.
source: The 5´-UGUA and AUA-3´ base specific interactions bracket a central region in which the 5th base turns away from the concave RNA-binding surface and stacks directly with the 4th base (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2C and 2D.

claim: The 5th base is not recognized by PUF-8, and PBE RNAs with any nucleotide at position 5 are bound by PUF-8 with similar affinity.
source: As a result, the 5th base is not recognized by PUF-8, and PBE RNAs with any nucleotide at position 5 are bound by PUF-8 with similar affinity (Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding affinity data presented in Table 2.

claim: R362 in R5 is located at the position that typically would form stacking interactions between the 4th and 5th RNA bases, but instead the side chain is moved aside.
source: R362 in R5 is located at the position that typically would form stacking interactions between the 4th and 5th RNA bases, but instead the side chain is moved aside (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2C and 2D.

claim: This type of recognition was observed in crystal structures of human PUM1 and PUM2 with some RNA sequences and is termed the base-omission mode.
source: This type of recognition was observed in crystal structures of human PUM1 and PUM2 with some RNA sequences and is termed the base-omission mode (Lu and Hall, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lu and Hall, 2011.

claim: The mode of RNA recognition and overall curvature of PUF-8 are reminiscent of the one repeat to one base modularity of PUM1.
source: The mode of RNA recognition and overall curvature of PUF-8 are reminiscent of the one repeat to one base modularity of PUM1 (Lu and Hall, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to PUM1 structure and a citation to Lu and Hall, 2011.

claim: Superposition of the structures highlights this relationship as the RMSD is 1.2 Å over 293 Cα atoms, and the inner RNA-binding helices align with similar curvature.
source: Superposition of the structures highlights this relationship as the RMSD is 1.2 Å over 293 Cα atoms, and the inner RNA-binding helices align with similar curvature (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison data and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: FBF-2 and PUF-8 do not superimpose well over all eight PUM repeats.
source: In contrast, FBF-2 and PUF-8 do not superimpose well over all eight PUM repeats.
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison.

claim: Aligning repeats R5-R8 illustrates that the curvature of the PUF-8 scaffold contrasts starkly with the flatter FBF-2 scaffold.
source: Aligning repeats R5-R8 illustrates that the curvature of the PUF-8 scaffold contrasts starkly with the flatter FBF-2 scaffold (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PUF-8 resembles PUM1 with respect to curvature and mode of RNA recognition.
source: These results indicate that PUF-8 resembles PUM1 with respect to curvature and mode of RNA recognition.
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison data.

claim: Repeat R5 of FBF-2 lies opposite the additional central nucleotides in the FBE RNA.
source: As noted above, repeat R5 of FBF-2 lies opposite the additional central nucleotides in the FBE RNA (Figures 1B and 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figures 1B and 2C.

claim: In the central region of both PUF-8 and PUM1, R5 uses its TRM to directly contact the RNA base at position 4.
source: In the central region of both PUF-8 and PUM1, R5 uses its TRM to directly contact the RNA base at position 4 (Figures 2C and 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figures 2C and 3A.

claim: The R5 TRMs of PUM1, PUF-8 and FBF-2 are identical, CQ/R.
source: Although the R5 TRMs of PUM1, PUF-8 and FBF-2 are identical, CQ/R (by convention C and Q are the edge-on residues and R is the stacking residue), we proposed that substitution of amino acid residues in the R5 TRM might produce interactions with the RNA that could favor binding of FBF-2 to an 8-nt sequence and offset the effects of curvature.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence comparison of TRMs.

claim: A modified yeast three-hybrid screen was developed to identify TRM variants that cause FBF-2 to bind preferentially to an 8-nt PBE versus a 9-nt FBE.
source: To test this hypothesis, we developed a modified yeast three-hybrid screen to identify TRM variants that cause FBF-2 to bind preferentially to an 8-nt PBE versus a 9-nt FBE.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental approach used.

claim: A reporter was expressed under the control of the lac operator containing the integral membrane protein Aga2p fused to 10 HA epitope tags.
source: We expressed a reporter under the control of the lac operator containing the integral membrane protein Aga2p fused to 10 HA epitope tags (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental system and is supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In this system, the strength of an interaction drives proportional changes in the level of cell surface expression of the antigen.
source: In this system, the strength of an interaction drives proportional changes in the level of cell surface expression of the antigen, and we enriched for cells with high surface antigen expression using anti-HA antibodies immobilized on metal-containing resin.
evidence: The claim describes the principle of the screening system.

claim: An FBF-2 variant bearing the SS/Y TRM at repeat R5 preferentially binds to an 8-nt PBE.
source: We selected and validated a single FBF-2 variant both functionally and structurally (Figure 3B,C). The variant bears an SS/Y TRM at repeat R5, and this imparted the ability to bind to the 8-nt PBE RNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by functional and structural data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: A library with randomized codons in the edge-on and stacking positions of FBF-2 repeat R5 was generated.
source: To identify this variant, we generated a library with randomized codons in the edge-on and stacking positions of FBF-2 repeat R5.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental approach.

claim: ~20,000 unique transformants were subjected to genetic and magnetic cell selection.
source: We subjected ~20,000 unique transformants to genetic and magnetic cell selection.
evidence: The claim describes the scale of the screening experiment.

claim: The FBF-2 variant with an SS/Y TRM preferentially bound to the PBE versus the FBE.
source: We found that the FBF-2 variant with an SS/Y TRM preferentially bound to the PBE versus the FBE.
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast three-hybrid assay data.

claim: FBF-2 with a wildtype R5 TRM binds preferentially to the FBE.
source: As controls, we confirmed that FBF-2 with a wildtype R5 TRM binds preferentially to the FBE and PUF-8 binds preferentially to the PBE.
evidence: The claim is supported by control experiments in the yeast three-hybrid assay.

claim: PUF-8 binds preferentially to the PBE.
source: As controls, we confirmed that FBF-2 with a wildtype R5 TRM binds preferentially to the FBE and PUF-8 binds preferentially to the PBE.
evidence: The claim is supported by control experiments in the yeast three-hybrid assay.

claim: The binding affinity of the SS/Y variant for the PBE (22.7 nM) was comparable to the affinity of wild-type PUF-8 for the PBE (25.9 nM) and FBF-2 WT for the FBE (19.3 nM).
source: The binding affinity of the SS/Y variant for the PBE (22.7 nM) was comparable to the affinity of wild-type PUF-8 for the PBE (25.9 nM) and FBF-2 WT for the FBE (19.3 nM).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding affinity measurements from electrophoretic mobility shift assays.

claim: A crystal structure of the R5 SS/Y variant in complex with a PBE RNA was determined.
source: To understand how variation of the FBF-2 R5 TRM converts binding preference to an 8-nt PBE RNA, we determined a crystal structure of the R5 SS/Y variant in complex with a PBE RNA (Table 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by crystallographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: The Y364 residue in the R5 TRM stacks between bases A4 and A5, which positions FBF-2's PUM repeat R5 opposite a single RNA base, A4.
source: we determined a crystal structure of the R5 SS/Y variant in complex with a PBE RNA (Table 1) and found that the Y364 residue in the R5 TRM stacks between bases A4 and A5, which positions FBF-2's PUM repeat R5 opposite a single RNA base, A4 (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In crystal structures of wild-type FBF-2 with 9-nt RNAs, the three central RNA bases of nucleotides 4–6 form a 'triple stack' of bases that is accommodated by the flexible arginine side chain at the stacking position of repeat R5.
source: In crystal structures of wild-type FBF-2 with 9-nt RNAs, the three central RNA bases of nucleotides 4–6 form a 'triple stack' of bases that is accommodated by the flexible arginine side chain at the stacking position of repeat R5 (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Y364 of the SS/Y variant occupies the space of the middle base of the triple stack, which allows interactions of repeats R5 and R4 with bases 4 and 5, respectively.
source: In a manner similar to PUM1, Y364 of the the SS/Y variant occupies the space of the middle base of the triple stack, which allows interactions of repeats R5 and R4 with bases 4 and 5, respectively (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3A and 3C.

claim: The two serine side chains (S363 and S367) contact the A4 base.
source: The two serine side chains (S363 and S367) contact the A4 base.
evidence: The claim is based on structural observations.

claim: S363 forms a van der Waals interaction at the C2 position, and S367 interacts via a water molecule at the N1 position.
source: S363 forms a van der Waals interaction at the C2 position, and S367 interacts via a water molecule at the N1 position.
evidence: The claim is based on structural observations of specific interactions.

claim: FBF-2 R5 SS/Y retained the same overall curvature in complex with an 8-nt as wildtype FBF-2 in complex with a 9-nt RNA.
source: FBF-2 R5 SS/Y retained the same overall curvature in complex with an 8-nt as wildtype FBF-2 in complex with a 9-nt RNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The change in identity of the TRM residues is sufficient for the transformation of binding site length specificity.
source: We conclude that the change in identity of the TRM residues is sufficient for the transformation of binding site length specificity.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on structural and functional data.

claim: The SS/Y TRM was identified in a PUM repeat from Naegleria gruberi.
source: We identified the SS/Y TRM in a PUM repeat from Naegleria gruberi (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The observation of the SS/Y TRM in nature implies that the combination of amino acid residues reported here from in vitro selection has also arisen through natural selection.
source: The observation of the SS/Y TRM in nature implies that the combination of amino acid residues reported here from in vitro selection has also arisen through natural selection.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the discovery of the SS/Y TRM in a natural protein.

claim: All of the mutants with edge-on alanine substitutions and a tyrosine stacking residue retained preferential binding to the 8-nt PBE over the 9-nt FBE.
source: Intriguingly, all of the mutants with edge-on alanine substitutions and a tyrosine stacking residue retained preferential binding to the 8-nt PBE over the 9-nt FBE (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: A crystal structure of the AS/Y variant in complex with PBE RNA was nearly identical to the SS/Y structure.
source: A crystal structure of the AS/Y variant in complex with PBE RNA was nearly identical to the SS/Y structure (Table 1 and Figures 3C and 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison data shown in Table 1 and Figures 3C and 4B.

claim: The FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y variant demonstrated preferential binding to the 8-nt PBE over the 9-nt FBE.
source: We also tested the binding preferences of an FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y variant that we identified as an in vivo substitution by genome engineering (see below). This variant demonstrated preferential binding to the 8-nt PBE over the 9-nt FBE, and a crystal structure confirms recognition of the 8-nt motif (Figure 4A,C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding data and structural data shown in Figure 4A, 4C, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The tyrosine stacking residue plays a prominent role in preferential binding of FBF-2 variants to the PBE.
source: These data suggest that the tyrosine stacking residue plays a prominent role in preferential binding of FBF-2 variants to the PBE.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on mutagenesis and binding data.

claim: Substituting the stacking residue with alanine reverted FBF-2 R5 SS/A to 9-nt FBE specificity, indicating the crucial role of Y364.
source: We substituted the stacking residue with alanine, which reverted FBF-2 R5 SS/A to 9-nt FBE specificity, indicating the crucial role of Y364 (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: When the WT stacking residue, R364, was restored, the resulting R5 SS/R variant poorly discriminated between the FBE and PBE.
source: When we restored the WT stacking residue, R364, the resulting R5 SS/R variant poorly discriminated between the FBE and PBE.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding data.

claim: A CQ/Y variant, which maintains WT edge-interacting residues, failed to bind either RNA.
source: However, a CQ/Y variant, which maintains WT edge-interacting residues, failed to bind either RNA (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mutation of the stacking residue from arginine to tyrosine is necessary to direct specificity towards the PBE but small residues in the edge-on positions are also required to completely switch specificity.
source: Collectively, our data suggest that mutation of the stacking residue from arginine to tyrosine is necessary to direct specificity towards the PBE but small residues in the edge-on positions are also required to completely switch specificity.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on mutagenesis and binding data.

claim: The PUF-8 variant R2 SE/H and the FBF-2 variants R5 SS/Y R2 SE/H, R5 AS/Y R2 SE/H, and R5 AQ/Y R2 SE/H bound preferentially to the 8-nt U7G RNA with an order of magnitude greater activity than to the shorter and longer elements.
source: We found that the PUF-8 variant R2 SE/H and the FBF-2 variants R5 SS/Y R2 SE/H, R5 AS/Y R2 SE/H, and R5 AQ/Y R2 SE/H bound preferentially to the 8-nt U7G RNA with an order of magnitude greater activity than to the shorter and longer elements.
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast three-hybrid binding data.

claim: The FBF-2 R5 TRM variants retain association to the 3´ end of target RNAs.
source: We therefore conclude that the FBF-2 R5 TRM variants retain association to the 3´ end of target RNAs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on compensatory mutation experiments.

claim: The FBF-2 variants R5 SS/Y, AS/Y, and AQ/Y bound the PBE with comparable activity to PUF-8 and retained specificity for a U3 base.
source: The FBF-2 variants R5 SS/Y, AS/Y, and AQ/Y bound the PBE with comparable activity to PUF-8 and retained specificity for a U3 base.
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast three-hybrid binding data.

claim: PUF-8 was selective for A at nucleotide 4.
source: At nucleotide 4, which is opposite repeat R5, PUF-8 was selective for A, as expected.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data.

claim: FBF-2 R5 SS/Y bound equally well to either an A or G at position 4, similar to WT FBF-2.
source: However, the FBF-2 R5 TRM variants were not as selective at this position. FBF-2 R5 SS/Y bound equally well to either an A or G at position 4, similar to WT FBF-2 (Bernstein, 2005), and the R5 AS/Y variant accommodated A4, G4 or U4.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data and a citation to Bernstein, 2005.

claim: The R5 AS/Y variant accommodated A4, G4 or U4.
source: FBF-2 R5 SS/Y bound equally well to either an A or G at position 4, similar to WT FBF-2 (Bernstein, 2005), and the R5 AS/Y variant accommodated A4, G4 or U4.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data.

claim: The R5 AQ/Y variant displayed preference for A4, although not as strictly as PUF-8.
source: The R5 AQ/Y variant displayed preference for A4, although not as strictly as PUF-8.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data.

claim: At nucleotide 5, all proteins preferred A5 and excluded G5.
source: Finally, at nucleotide 5, all proteins preferred A5 and excluded G5.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data.

claim: PUF-8 had broadened specificity and also accommodated C5 or U5.
source: PUF-8 had broadened specificity and also accommodated C5 or U5, and FBF-2 R5 AS/Y and AQ/Y also bound to U5.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data.

claim: FBF-2 R5 AS/Y and AQ/Y also bound to U5.
source: PUF-8 had broadened specificity and also accommodated C5 or U5, and FBF-2 R5 AS/Y and AQ/Y also bound to U5.
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data.

claim: The FBF-2 R5 TRM variants retain specificity for U3 and the ability of WT FBF-2 to recognize A4 or G4.
source: Collectively, these experiments demonstrate that the FBF-2 R5 TRM variants retain specificity for U3 and the ability of WT FBF-2 to recognize A4 or G4.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on binding specificity data.

claim: The TRM variation at repeat R5 has differing effects on the specificity of repeat R4 for the nucleotide at position 5.
source: However, the TRM variation at repeat R5 has differing effects on the specificity of repeat R4 for the nucleotide at position 5.
evidence: The claim is based on binding specificity data.

claim: There is cooperativity between TRMs as opposed to true independent modularity.
source: This suggests that there is cooperativity between TRMs as opposed to true independent modularity.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that TRM variation at one repeat affects specificity at an adjacent repeat.

claim: The FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y variant demonstrates a recognition pattern qualitatively more similar to PUF-8 than FBF-2.
source: Finally, the FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y variant demonstrates a recognition pattern qualitatively more similar to PUF-8 than FBF-2.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on binding specificity data.

claim: Loss of puf-8 does not substantially impair mitotic proliferation or entry into meiosis in the C. elegans germline.
source: In the C. elegans germline, loss of puf-8 does not substantially impair mitotic proliferation or entry into meiosis (Subramaniam and Seydoux, 2003; Bachorik and Kimble, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Subramaniam and Seydoux, 2003 and Bachorik and Kimble, 2005.

claim: Temperature-sensitive germline proliferation-1 (glp-1) gain-of-function mutants have mitotic cells that overproliferate, resulting in a tumorous phenotype at the restrictive temperature (25°C).
source: This is in contrast with temperature-sensitive germline proliferation-1 (glp-1) gain-of-function mutants where mitotic cells overproliferate (e.g. the glp-1(ar202) strain), resulting in a tumorous phenotype at the restrictive temperature (25°C) (Pepper et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pepper et al., 2003.

claim: This phenotype is strongly enhanced by loss of puf-8 as evidenced by tumors at the permissive temperature (15°C).
source: This phenotype is strongly enhanced by loss of puf-8 as evidenced by tumors at the permissive temperature (15°C) (Racher and Hansen, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Racher and Hansen, 2012.

claim: Upon reduction of puf-8 by RNAi (puf-8(RNAi)), the glp-1(ar202) mutant strain develops tumors throughout the germline at permissive temperature (15°C).
source: Upon reduction of puf-8 by RNAi (puf-8(RNAi)), the glp-1(ar202) mutant strain develops tumors throughout the germline at permissive temperature (15°C) (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 98% of the glp-1(ar202) puf-8(RNAi) germlines contained tumors despite expression of WT FBF.
source: Based on these criteria, 98% of the glp-1(ar202) puf-8(RNAi) germlines contained tumors despite expression of WT FBF (Table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic analysis data presented in Table 3.

claim: Tumor formation in the glp-1(ar202) animals depended upon depletion of puf-8, since treatment of animals with an RNAi vector containing a scrambled RNA sequence did not result in tumorigenesis.
source: Tumor formation in the glp-1(ar202) animals depended upon depletion of puf-8, since treatment of animals with an RNAi vector containing a scrambled RNA sequence did not result in tumorigenesis (Table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by control experiment data presented in Table 3.

claim: A C. elegans strain expressing an 8-nt-binding FBF-2 variant was generated using CRISPR.
source: To test this idea, we generated a C. elegans strain expressing an 8-nt-binding FBF-2 variant using CRISPR.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental approach.

claim: Mutations were introduced into the endogenous gene encoding FBF-2.
source: Mutations were introduced into the endogenous gene encoding FBF-2 (note that FBF-2 can be modified, because FBF-1 is functionally redundant to FBF-2).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental approach.

claim: A single strain that incorporated a novel repeat R5 TRM variant - AQ/Y was recovered.
source: We did, however, recover multiple strains with deletion mutations and a single strain that incorporated a novel repeat R5 TRM variant - AQ/Y.
evidence: The claim describes the outcome of the genome editing experiment.

claim: This mutant strain was designated fbf-2(lot14).
source: This mutant strain was designated fbf-2(lot14).
evidence: The claim provides the strain designation.

claim: The AQ/Y mutation preferentially binds to the PBE relative to the FBE in cells and in vitro.
source: Serendipitously, as shown above, the AQ/Y mutation preferentially binds to the PBE relative to the FBE in cells and in vitro (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Table 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by binding data shown in Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Table 2.

claim: A crystal structure of the FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y variant bound to the PBE adopts a similar conformation to SS/Y and AS/Y bound to the PBE.
source: and a crystal structure of the FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y variant bound to the PBE adopts a similar conformation to SS/Y and AS/Y bound to the PBE (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y mutant retains base recognition specificity at flanking positions.
source: Furthermore, the FBF-2 R5 AQ/Y mutant retains base recognition specificity at flanking positions (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding specificity data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The AQ/Y variant behaves similarly to SS/Y and AS/Y and preferentially favors binding to the 8-nt PBE.
source: We conclude that the AQ/Y variant behaves similarly to SS/Y and AS/Y and preferentially favors binding to the 8-nt PBE.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on binding and structural data.

claim: The edited strain expressing the FBF-2 AQ/Y variant (fbf-2(lot-14), glp-1(ar202) animals) displayed tumor formation in only 36% of gonads at 15°C.
source: We found that the edited strain expressing the FBF-2 AQ/Y variant (fbf-2(lot-14), glp-1(ar202) animals) displayed tumor formation in only 36% of gonads at 15°C (Figure 6B, Table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic analysis data shown in Figure 6B and Table 3.

claim: Tumors were formed in 98% of gonads from glp-1(ar202) animals.
source: In contrast, tumors were formed in 98% of gonads from glp-1(ar202) animals (Figure 6A, Table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic analysis data shown in Figure 6A and Table 3.

claim: The FBF-2 AQ/Y variant is capable of substituting for PUF-8 in vivo.
source: Thus, the FBF-2 AQ/Y variant is capable of substituting for PUF-8 in vivo.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the rescue of the tumor phenotype.

claim: PUF-8 adopts a structure reminiscent of human PUM1 and forms base-specific contacts to seven of the eight nucleotides that comprise the binding element.
source: Our experiments reveal three insights into RNA-PUF protein interactions. First, PUF-8 adopts a structure reminiscent of human PUM1 and forms base-specific contacts to seven of the eight nucleotides that comprise the binding element.
evidence: The claim is a summary of structural findings.

claim: Mutations in repeat 5 of FBF-2 can introduce new contacts to the RNA that switch preferential binding to an 8-nt PBE sequence motif over a 9-nt FBE motif.
source: Second, mutations in repeat 5 of FBF-2 can introduce new contacts to the RNA that switch preferential binding to an 8-nt PBE sequence motif over a 9-nt FBE motif.
evidence: The claim is a summary of mutagenesis and binding findings.

claim: The amino acid residue combinations obtained through random mutagenesis occur in nature.
source: The amino acid residue combinations we obtained through random mutagenesis occur in nature.
evidence: The claim is based on the identification of the SS/Y TRM in N. gruberi.

claim: A variation in FBF-2 that enables it to recognize the consensus binding element of PUF-8 rescues a germline tumor phenotype caused by loss of function of puf-8 in a sensitized background.
source: Third and finally, a variation in FBF-2 that enables it to recognize the consensus binding element of PUF-8 rescues a germline tumor phenotype caused by loss of function of puf-8 in a sensitized background.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the in vivo functional rescue experiment.

claim: The identities of the TRMs contribute to the RNA motif length of PUF proteins.
source: Prior results suggest that the degree of curvature of the RNA-binding surface of PUF proteins corresponds to the length of the RNA element that is recognized, but our results here indicate that the identities of the TRMs also contribute to the RNA motif length of PUF proteins.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: A minimum of two amino acid changes (CQ/R to AQ/Y) can swap binding element length preference, but they do not impact curvature.
source: In the case of changing specificity of FBF-2 to that of PUF-8, we have demonstrated that a minimum of two amino acid changes (CQ/R to AQ/Y) can swap binding element length preference, but they do not impact curvature.
evidence: The claim is based on mutagenesis and structural data.

claim: Changes in curvature are remarkably well correlated with, but not necessarily required for alterations in binding element length preference.
source: This finding is consistent with the notion that changes in curvature are remarkably well correlated with, but not necessarily required for alterations in binding element length preference.
